key_highlights: ASX shed $90bn in a week as rate-rise fears and oil price surge pressured miners and banks
Iron ore entering a 'bloodletting' phase, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX
AUD smashed on growth scare; fuel prices set to rise 30c/litre
RBA flagged rental inflation as key concern, complicating rate path
ANZ.AX restructuring 3,500 jobs but strategic plan still unproven
Housing prices crashing while first-home buyers surge; auction market showing no spring bounce
Australia softened local gas supply rules, easing Asian energy fears (Santos, Woodside positive)
Mining cap raises accelerating via Canaccord-led dash for cash

sectors.trend: Sharp negative. Iron ore 'bloodletting' underway; ASX miners leading the $90bn weekly sell-off. Cap raises accelerating as juniors seek cash. Gold underperforming ('gold schmould').
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin compression. Junior miners (PolarX, Sunstone, Manuka) showing relative strength but cap-raise dilution risk rising. Aruma, Iondrive among ASX runners.

sectors.trend: Negative. Banks tumbling alongside miners. ANZ.AX post-3,500-job cut still faces execution risk. Rising bond yields and rate fears pressure net interest margins.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX, ANZ.AX under pressure. Rising yields could support NIMs but credit risk and growth scare dominate. Superannuation policy debate adds uncertainty.

sectors.trend: Mixed-positive. Oil 'explodes' as price suppression fails; Australia softens gas supply rules easing Asian fears. Santos preservation seen as national priority. Fuel prices rising 30c.
sectors.implications: Santos (STO.AX) and Woodside (WDS.AX) benefit from gas policy easing. Higher oil supports upstream but 30c fuel hike pressures consumer spending and transport costs.

sectors.trend: Negative. Woolworths (WES.AX) caught raising 'family staple' prices during Price Freeze. Australian businesses fearing for future. Gen Z burnout stalling earning power.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WOW.AX face margin pressure from input costs. Consumer confidence deteriorating. Defensive staples may see rotation but pricing power questioned.

sectors.trend: Negative. Housing prices crashing, auction market flat. RBA worried about rental inflation. Property chiefs calling for more migrants. NZ correction still running.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) face rental yield compression. Housing correction may extend 6-12 months. First-home buyer surge could support volume but not prices.

sectors.trend: Neutral-positive. CSL.AX relatively insulated. ASX small-caps (Neurizon, Australasian) showing momentum. Global AI/tech themes (Anthropic IPO, Ciena backlog) supportive.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX offer defensive exposure. Small-cap tech/biotech (Neurizon, Australasian) benefiting from risk-on pockets despite broad sell-off.

Iron ore structural decline pressuring ASX 20 heavyweights
AUD weakness amplifying import costs and fuel prices
RBA caught between rental inflation and growth scare
Housing market correction accelerating across Australia and NZ
Mining sector cap-raise dilution cycle intensifying
Superannuation policy under political and structural scrutiny
Energy policy shift (gas supply rules) as positive for ASX energy names

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce exposure to BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX; diversify into gold and critical minerals

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate path uncertainty / rental inflation
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge duration risk; favour floating-rate REITs; monitor RBA statements closely

risk_assessment.risk_factor: AUD depreciation and fuel cost inflation
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight exporters; underweight import-dependent consumer staples
Avoid construction and home-loan-heavy financials; monitor auction clearance rates
Avoid junior miners with imminent raises; favour cash-flow-positive producers

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Global growth scare / Fed rate hike
risk_assessment.mitigation: Maintain cash buffer; favour domestic defensive equities (CSL.AX, WES.AX)

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight ASX energy names on gas policy easing and oil surge
opportunities.rationale: Softened gas supply rules and oil price spike support STO.AX, WDS.AX earnings; Asian demand secured

opportunities.recommendation: Selective exposure to ASX small-cap momentum names
opportunities.rationale: Neurizon, Australasian, Aruma showing relative strength; Iondrive in critical minerals

opportunities.recommendation: Add defensive healthcare on broad sell-off
opportunities.rationale: CSL.AX insulated from commodity/rate cycles; global demand stable

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore and thermal coal exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore 'bloodletting' underway; structural demand shift; cap-raise dilution risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge AUD weakness and rate risk
defensive_moves.rationale: AUD smashed on growth scare; RBA rental inflation concern complicates cuts; rising yields pressure equities
Housing crash, flat auctions, Woolworths price-hike scandal, business confidence deteriorating

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish. ASX likely to test lower supports as iron ore weakness, AUD depreciation, and rate fears persist. Oil spike provides partial offset for energy names. Expect volatility around RBA commentary and US Fed signals. $90bn weekly loss suggests further downside before stabilisation.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive. Housing correction may create entry points in 6-12 months. Gas policy reform supports energy sector. Critical minerals and battery tech (Critical Resources) offer structural growth. Superannuation reform debate could unlock capital flows. Key risk: prolonged iron ore downturn and global growth slowdown.
